findings.statement: Higher TUFM expression in sigmoid colon raises UC risk, odds ratio per SD [gene=TUFM; type=mendelian_randomization_gut; source=DATASET:MR_GUT_EQTL_UC; layer=colon_tissue; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.191], colocalising with the IBD GWAS and replicating in FinnGen and Liu 2023. In IBDverse plasma B cells the odds ratio per SD is [gene=TUFM; type=mendelian_randomization_gut; source=DATASET:MR_GUT_EQTL_UC; layer=gut_cell; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.356], also colocalising and replicating, so inhibition is the therapeutic direction. It has a single instrument (Steiger direction correct; Egger and weighted median not computable), and its Open Targets association ranks outside the top 150 of the genes in the graph.

The genetic-target record gives a fine-mapped UC signal (tier confident) whose risk allele raises TUFM expression, predicted mainly in blood neutrophil and colon myeloid cells; biopsies show no change.

INHBA has an approved inhibitor in another disease (pulmonary arterial hypertension) and none tried in UC or IBD, which makes it a repurposing candidate. It is strongly loss-constrained, LOEUF [gene=INHBA; type=target_safety; source=DATASET:SAFETY; loeuf=0.166], with no curated safety events.
CFB has an approved inhibitor for IgA glomerulonephritis and paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria, none tried in UC or IBD. It is not loss-constrained and has no curated safety events.

SELP has an approved inhibitor in sickle cell anaemia and none tried in UC. Plasma-protein MR is null, p [gene=SELP; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; p=0.484], and does not replicate in FinnGen or Liu 2023, so genetics give no support for SELP in UC.

LY96 (MD-2) has a phase 3 inhibitor in sepsis and covid-19 and none in UC. Plasma MR (two instruments) is not significant and does not replicate in FinnGen; gut cell MR (non-classical monocytes) is also not significant.

CHI3L1 genetics do not support it: plasma MR is not significant and does not replicate in FinnGen, and colon-tissue MR is also not significant. The literature is split between pathogenic and protective mouse results (knockout worsens colitis), so inhibition has a possible mucosal-protection risk.

MMP10 plasma MR is not significant (higher protein tends to raise risk but without replication), no gut instrument exists, and the literature is split between protective and pathogenic mouse results, so genetics and mouse evidence do not clearly support inhibition.

SERPINB5 has two independent mouse colitis papers in which knockdown or ablation protects (pathogenic role), and it is intrinsically epithelial. It has no genetic instrument, so human genetics are untested.

CEBPB gut-cell MR (progenitor enterocytes) is not significant after correction and does not replicate in FinnGen; it points the opposite way to the genetic-target hypothesis (higher expression lowers risk), so the pool's inhibit hypothesis is not backed by MR.
RORC comes only from a sequence-predicted genetic-target record with a tiny predicted effect and has no MR support (not significant or not testable).
CFAP90 is a confident-tier predicted-expression signal with no MR support and no biopsy change.
FIGNL1 is a confident-tier predicted-expression signal in NK cells with no MR support and no biopsy change.
CPXM1 (first-in-class) is a stromal gene with an antibody route and a thin UC literature; it is expression-led.

caveats: Most first-in-class and known-list genes (CHRDL2, PCDH17, LILRA1, SGIP1, FIBIN, XKR9, FJX1, OLFML2B, CEACAM4, CYP4X1, SDR16C5, LYPD5, KLK10, REG1B, CXCL1, CXCL3, PDPN, GUCY1A1, LAIR2) were not individually queried in the external tools.
No cis-pQTL or gut eQTL for CFB, INHBA, MMP10 (gut) or CHI3L1 (gut cell): not tested is not evidence against.
Drug names were left out because no drug_literature record was retrieved.
The TUFM MR has a single instrument.
